research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register original (47 FR 12785, PDF pages 9-10) is Executive Order 12353 of March 23, 1982, Ronald Reagan, Charitable Fund-Raising (the Combined Federal Campaign). The packet inventory had three clauses (sections 1-4 lumped, 5, 6) and omitted sections 7, 8 and 9 and the preamble; it is corrected by overrides to ten clauses: preamble and sections 1 to 9. Later instruments: EO 12404 (February 10, 1983) replaced section 1, added subsection designation (a) and new subsection (b) principles to section 2, and continued existing rules; EO 13743 (October 13, 2016) changed agencies to voluntary health and welfare organizations in the preamble and sections 2 and 3, replaced sections 1, 5 and 6, rewrote section 2(b)(5), and continued existing rules. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 1101 prints the order as amended by those two orders only (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) with sections 3, 4, 7 and 8 unchanged and section 9 revoking Executive Order 10927; other Code notes (2 U.S.C. 4524, 4557 and 4558) cite it and the eCFR search found 19 mentions (leads only). No held instrument revokes it.
savings_reason: No clause ended, so there is nothing to save; rules, regulations and directives issued under the order were expressly continued by EO 12404 section 2 and EO 13743 section 2(d) until revoked or modified, and the bounded searches name no revocation.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER":"The machine lead is a 2007-08-28 Federal Register rule (document E7-16986, 72 FR 49195) in the selden-fr-citers citation list, classified as a revocation of this order; its sentence says only that references to Executive Order 10927 are obsolete because that order was revoked by Executive Order No. 12353 issued March 23, 1982. It therefore records the revocation of EO 10927 by section 9 of this order and is not a revocation of EO 12353; it ends no clause of this order."}
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order's number: EDGES, the U.S. Code notes and the OFR notes show only EO 12404 and EO 13743 (both amendments) and a court-case See reference (Cornelius v. NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund, 473 U.S. 788 (1985), a decision upholding the order's exclusion rules, which does not end the order). The 2007 Federal Register rule E7-16986 (72 FR 49195) that the claim-drafts conflict list reads as a partial ending is a statement that EO 10927 was revoked by this order, not a revocation of this order. The chain items typed revoke for EO 12404 section 2 and EO 13743 section 2(d) are continuity clauses that keep rules issued under EO 12353 in effect until modified; they do not revoke the order. The order has no duration or sunset of its own.
scope_check: Ten clauses: the preamble, and sections 1 (OPM Director arranges the annual Combined Federal Campaign), 2 (eligibility criteria), 3 (consultation), 4 (arrangement requirements: voluntary contributions, solicitation period, one solicitation a year), 5 (local campaign authority), 6 (solicitation forms), 7 (exclusion of member solicitations by employee organizations), 8 (Director to prescribe rules) and 9 (revocation of EO 10927 with a saving of its directives). All remain in force as amended.
independent_command_check: Each section is an independent command and each was either amended in place (sections 1, 2, 3, 5, 6) or left unchanged (4, 7, 8, 9); none was ended. Section 9's revocation of EO 10927 stands and its saving of directives issued under that order continues until modified, which no held source shows to have happened.

research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register original (49 FR 22053, PDF page 23) is Executive Order 12478 of May 23, 1984, Ronald Reagan, Transfer of Authority to the Secretary of State To Make Reimbursements for Protection of Foreign Missions to International Organizations; the four inventory clauses are sections 1 to 4 (section 4 is effective on October 1, 1984). Current law: the authority transferred came from former 3 U.S.C. 202(7) and 208(a), recodified by Pub. L. 109-177 title VI section 605(a) (March 9, 2006) at 18 U.S.C. 3056A(a)(7) and (d); the held text of 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d) says the authority of that subsection may be transferred by the President to the Secretary of State and that in carrying out duties under paragraphs (7) and (9) the Secretary of State may use authority under title II of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (Foreign Missions Act), and the held savings provision, Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b), says that title does not affect any Executive order transferring to the Secretary of State the authority of section 208 of title 3 in effect on the day before March 9, 2006. The held U.S. Code note under 18 U.S.C. 3056A prints this order with the former section numbers marked, and no ending. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order.
savings_reason: The only transfer that is a completed act is section 2 (unexpended moneys appropriated to the Department of the Treasury for reimbursements under former 3 U.S.C. 208(a)), which took effect with the order on October 1, 1984 and was not reversed; the authority transferred by section 1 continues, so nothing has lapsed that needs saving. The exact amount transferred is not held and is not claimed.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order's number: the EDGES file, the U.S. Code note under 18 U.S.C. 3056A and the other held texts return no amendment, revocation or supersession of this order, and the OFR codification notes show it only as codified in 22 CFR chapter material. The only own-terms date is section 4, effective October 1, 1984, a start date and not an end; sections 1 to 3 have no duration or condition.
scope_check: Four clauses, one per section: section 1 transfers to the Secretary of State the authority to determine need for and approve terms of reimbursable extraordinary protective activities for foreign diplomatic missions and to reimburse State and local governments; section 2 transfers the unexpended appropriated moneys; section 3 requires coordination with protective security programs under the Foreign Missions Act of 1982; section 4 makes the order effective on October 1, 1984.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (the transferred authority) is independent of section 2 (the money): the authority was saved by Pub. L. 109-177 section 606(b) and continues in 18 U.S.C. 3056A(d); section 2 was a one-time transfer of whatever unexpended moneys existed when the order took effect, which no later instrument undoes; section 3 is a continuing coordination duty tied to section 1; section 4 fixed the start date.

research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register original (26 FR 11937, PDF page 3) is Executive Order 10979, signed by John F. Kennedy on December 12, 1961, amending Executive Order 10717 of June 27, 1957 (the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service) by substituting new sections 2, 7 and 8. The packet inventory lumped section 2(b), section 7 and section 8 into the last item clause; it is corrected by overrides into the lead, section 2(a), section 2(b), section 7 and section 8, because their fates differ. EO 12014 (October 19, 1977) abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and amended EO 10717 by deleting sections 3 through 9 and adding new sections 3 and 4; sections 7 and 8 (the Board's nomination form and its guidance) therefore ended on 1977-10-19, the nomination principles reappearing in new section 4 of EO 10717. Sections 2(a) and 2(b) were not touched: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 4504 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints section 2(a)-(b) of EO 10717 in the same words as this order and shows EO 10717 as amended through EO 12107 with no ending.
savings_reason: EO 12014 deleted sections 7 and 8 and in the same sentence added new sections 3 and 4 of EO 10717 carrying the nomination procedure and the concurrence and career-position principles to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, so the functions were transferred rather than lost; no award made under the order is invalidated by either instrument.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for this order's number and for EO 10717: the only instruments reaching EO 10717 are EO 11085 (1963, terms of Board members in section 4 and other award matters), EO 12014 (1977) and EO 12107 (1978, agency-name substitutions); only EO 12014 reaches sections 7 and 8, so it is the first end of those two clauses. No earlier revocation or own-terms end of sections 2, 7 or 8 exists (the order has no duration or condition), and nothing revokes EO 10717 or EO 10979 as a whole.
scope_check: Five clauses by correction: the amending lead (authority and substitution command), section 2(a) (the award, its criteria (1)-(4)), section 2(b) (importance of achievement, five awards a year), section 7 (Board nominations and agency-head concurrence) and section 8 (Board guidance and the career-position limit). The first-ended clauses are sections 7 and 8 only; the lead and section 2 remain.
independent_command_check: Section 2 is an independent command (who receives the award and on what achievements) and was not ended with the Board. research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register original (51 FR 24299, PDF page 13) is Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986, Ronald Reagan, Delegating Certain Functions of the President Relating to Federal Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses. Three sections: section 1 amends section 1 of Executive Order 10621 (redesignating subsection (i) as (g), revoking (o), adding subsection (h) on the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5702(a) for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and possessions); section 2 delegates the same authority for areas outside the United States to the Secretary of State; section 3 revokes Executive Order 11294. Current law: the held text of 5 U.S.C. 5702(a)(1)(A)-(B) still gives the President or his designee the power to set per diem and actual-expense limits for travel outside the continental United States; the held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 prints EO 10621 as amended through EO 12561 with subsection (h) in the current text, and the note under 5 U.S.C. 5702 prints this order, both through release point 119-121 (2026-10-09), with no ending. No later amendment or revocation is held.

The order has no duration or condition, so no own-terms end exists.

The packet inventory did not match the text (it contained duplicated sub-items such as sec5-b-dup2 and sec5-i-ii); it is corrected by overrides to eleven section-level clauses. Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 prints the order as amended by EO 14085 section 5 with no ending (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). No instrument revokes it.
